sourceInformation.genre: Arcade space shooter with sector strategy and rescue missions
sourceInformation.perspective: Third-person chase camera; tactical sector map
sourceInformation.tech: Three.js r180 WebGPURenderer / TSL (WebGPU preferred, WebGL 2 fallback); Rapier 0.19.3; Web Audio; Gamepad API; PeerJS 1.5.5; AI Hub Session Protocol v1 client 1.4.0; HTML/CSS/JavaScript
sourceInformation.artDirection: Procedural low-poly cel shading with stepped TSL lighting, ink edges, cream/coral/cyan palette, ringed planets and alien horizons
sourceInformation.animation: Three.js AnimationMixer, AnimationClip and keyframe tracks for engine pulses, wing flex, rescue beacons and boss aperture; procedural flight motion
sourceInformation.audio: Original code-generated synthesizer music at 10% by default; procedural sound effects; formant-filtered Animalese/Simlish-style gibberish; no audio files
sourceInformation.online: 1–2 player shared-world co-op; AI Hub host-authoritative sessions including dedicated host; standalone PeerJS WebRTC rooms and same-origin BroadcastChannel
sourceInformation.testing: One-command headless suite: complete campaign with real Rapier collisions and test invulnerability; keyboard/mouse; emulated standard gamepad; iPhone-profile touch; Web Audio levels; 2-tab co-op and replicated audio; AI Hub standard, host-leave, dedicated server and post-end input; forced graphics-device recovery; file:// launch; WebGL fallback screenshots. Physical controllers and real mobile/WAN devices: unknown.
sourceInformation.research: Original Atari instruction manual, AtariAge screenshots, MobyGames credits/overview, official Three.js and Rapier documentation, AI Hub protocol and harness. Exact original audio patches unknown.
sourceInformation.environment: Codex CLI (headless); Linux / Ubuntu 26.04 on WSL2

testingFeedback: Testing and review found 13 confirmed issues, all fixed: planet attachment, mouse projection, guest touch routing, guest lobby transition, duplicate Enter activation, reconnect sequence tracking, target-lock consistency, disconnect recovery, graphics-device recovery, post-round input, guest scanner isolation, co-op audio replication, and controller prompts after slider input. Final automated suite: 122/122 checks passed.
2 confirmed game-breaking issues: the guest co-op lobby could block flight input after launch, and graphics initialization could stall after native WebGPU device loss. Both are fixed.

Deliberately forcing graphics-device loss exposed a null WebGL context during recovery. The complete campaign test also verified all six sectors, eleven rescues, the key and door, refuelling, boss phases and victory through real Rapier collisions.
Static JavaScript syntax checks: useful for packaging, but they could not reveal visual or gameplay problems.
engineFeedback: Three.js TSL makes stepped cel lighting and procedural geometry straightforward, with AnimationMixer for reusable clips.

I initially blocked readiness on full shader warm-up. Concurrent headless Chromium WebGPU devices can be lost; removing the warm-up and adding bounded initialization plus graphics recovery made readiness reliable. Visual checks used WebGL 2 captures while live state verified WebGPU.
The campaign state machine, arcade flight and combat rules, controller-first menus, host-authoritative co-op replication, and graphics-device recovery.
Reliable asynchronous graphics initialization and headless verification: concurrent software WebGPU devices can disappear, so startup and recovery need explicit handling.
none; the engine source is unchanged. Recovery, shaders and gameplay are application code.
A first-class deterministic headless render-and-readback path for WebGPU.
promptFeedback: The source research, complete vertical-slice scope, procedural audio and controller-first requirements provide a clear creative direction.
AI Hub integration is specified, but standalone signalling and NAT traversal are not. I chose PeerJS public signalling with direct peer transport. No plan file was supplied; recorded none.
Making sector strategy, rescue, keyed corridors, combat and co-op feel like one coherent arcade patrol.
Specify a target demo duration and whether standalone online rooms require a bundled signalling service or may use a public broker.

aiHub.name: Solaris Detour
aiHub.tagline: One lost planet. A galaxy of trouble.
aiHub.description: Take the scenic route through an inked galaxy: defend an uplink, rescue stranded cadets, unlock an ion corridor, and find Solaris. Fly solo or bring a wingmate to take down the Sun Eater.
aiHub.controls: WASD / left stick: fly; mouse / right stick: aim; click, Space / R2: fire; Shift / L2: boost; E / Square: nova pulse; M / Triangle: scanner; Esc / Options: pause. Touch: left drag fly, right drag aim, auto-fire.
